text:
mia_support: FYI customer ACME sent a bunch of 429s right after our limit push at 03:00 UTC. They say it happened for a single API key and then recovered. Can we check canary rollout?

alex_platform: Looking now. We ramped the new per-key burst cap (tokens/min) at 03:00 in region eu-west-1 in the phased rollout. Can you share their key id?

mia_support: key=ak_live_XXX123 (redacted). They reported: 'sudden 429s for ~10m, then traffic resumed but with higher latency for some requests.'

jon_oncall: Pulling logs. I see a flood of short-lived 429s from that key between 03:02-03:11. Error message is our standard rate_limit_exceeded. No auth failures.

ryan_sre: Any chance the client retried aggressively and tripped global burst smoothing? We have a smoothing window that will transiently reduce capacity if burst traffic looks pathological.

mia_support: Customer claims they didn't change behavior. They showed a spike of parallel requests from their ingestion worker at 03:01.

alex_platform: Can you paste the rollout config? I pushed a gradual toggle: 
```yaml
policy: per_key_burst
initial: 10r/s
burst_window: 60s
ramp: [10%,25%,50%,100%]
regions: [global,eu-west-1]
```
Ramp target for eu-west-1 should have been 25% at 03:00, not 100. Investigating if the rollout engine skipped a step.

deploy-bot: deploy 235d8f1 to infra-rate-limiter completed at 02:58 UTC (canary group: 2/5).

jon_oncall: Hmm deploy shows 2/5 canaries healthy then immediate scale to 5/5 at 03:00 by autoscaler. That might have accelerated the policy flip.

alex_platform: If autoscaler forced all nodes live, rollout engine may have considered canary healthy and advanced. Need to check rollout controller logs for promotion decision.

ryan_sre: For mitigation: we can rollback the per-key burst change or temporarily relax burst_window to avoid aggressive smoothing. Which is lowest risk?

sara_custsuccess: Customer wants immediate relief — they offered to pause ingestion for 15m if we prefer a controlled rollback. They prefer we fix server-side.

mia_support: Can we do a soft rollback to previous limit for that single key while we investigate?

alex_platform: Yes, we can apply an override to that key via the runtime override table. Command: 
```
rlctl override add --key ak_live_XXX123 --policy per_key_burst --limit 100r/m --reason "support mitigation"
```
That should bypass the new staged policy. I'll run it now.

alex_platform: Done. Override applied at 03:18 UTC. Notifying customer.

mia_support: ACME confirms requests are succeeding again. Thanks. They still report a few slow responses (200s) for long prompts.

jon_oncall: Latency traces show KV cache misses around same time — likely due to concurrent cold workers. Not caused by auth.

ryan_sre: For root cause hypothesis: rollout acceleration + autoscaler + client's sudden fan-out triggered burst-smoothing and per-key limit then 429s. We need to (1) add a safety gate so rollout promotion doesn't occur while autoscale is in progress, (2) add a canary traffic sample check for parallel request patterns, and (3) improve per-key override tooling.

alex_platform: Agreed. I'll open an RFC and a follow-up ticket: rollout-controller: add 'suspend-promotion-while-scaling' + sample-based canary checks.

mia_support: I'll follow up with ACME and offer a short credit and the override until fix lands.

sara_custsuccess: Please include repro steps for eng: they want a small script to reproduce with parallel workers.

jon_oncall: Repro snippet I used (stress 50 concurrent, each does 1 req/s):
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do
  (while true; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ak_live_XXX123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 0.9; done) &
done
wait
```
This reproduces 429s locally against the canary cluster.

ryan_sre: I'll attach graphs: token-rate, 429-rate, latency-p50/p95, autoscaler events. Add them to the incident ticket.

alex_platform: Ticket created: INF-4821. Assigning to rollout-controller + rate-limiter. Labels: canary-accel, per-key-override, autoscale-interaction.

mia_support: Team — thanks. Document mitigation steps in the ticket and tag me when there's a plan so I can close the customer loop. :thumbsup:

sara_custsuccess: I'll draft the customer note once we have change timeline.

deploy-bot: rollback 235d8f1 scheduled? No. (manual rollback required)

jon_oncall: Postmortem candidate if we find the rollout logic bug. For now, monitoring alarms: raise alert when a single key > 100 429s in 5m after a policy flip.

alex_platform: Copy that. Setting alert and timeline for RFC: 48h for hotfix, 2w for full rollout-controller changes.

mia_support: closing loop: ACME accepted credit and override, will monitor. Thanks everyone.
